The entropy change for 1 g of nitrogen (n = 1/28 mol, cp = 7 cal/(mol·K)) cooling from 20°C (293 K) to -196°C (77 K) at constant pressure is ΔS = n cp ln(T2/T1) = 0.25 × ln(77/293) ≈ -0.334 cal/K.

For the spherical iron ball (radius 20 cm, thermal diffusivity α = 0.185 cm²/s), the center temperature after 15 min (900 s) with surface at 0°C and initial uniform 100°C is given by T_center = 0 + 100 × 2 e^{-π²αt/R²} with αt/R² = 0.41625, giving T_center ≈ 3.29°C.

For the window glass (thickness 2 mm, k = 2×10⁻³ cal/(s·cm·°C), convection flux q = 4×10⁻⁵ (Δt)^{5/4}), the inner surface temperature satisfies 2ΔT + 0.004 ΔT^{5/4} = 40 with ΔT = 25 – T_in. Solving yields ΔT ≈ 19.916°C, so T_in ≈ 5.08°C.
